## Quality Testing, Compliance, and Procurement Terms

For bag-grade PP spunbond, the lab parameters that matter to a serious manufacturer are GSM tolerance (±3%), tensile strength MD/CD (target > 80/60 N/5cm at 60 GSM), elongation (≥ 35%), and colour fastness (rating 4–5 on grey scale). For export-bound bags, REACH and CPSIA documentation is increasingly demanded by EU and US retailers. Favourite Fab supplies CoA with every roll and supports third-party lab testing on request — a non-negotiable for tender and modern trade supply.

Common procurement mistakes among new bag manufacturers: ordering on price-per-kg alone without checking actual GSM yield (a “cheap” 58 GSM roll sold as 60 GSM costs you 3.3% more bags-per-kg loss), specifying narrow colour ranges that lock you into single-supplier dependency, and ignoring roll-width compatibility with your bag-making machine. ## Frequently Asked Questions

**What material are non-woven bags made from?**

Non-woven bags are most commonly made from PP (polypropylene) spunbond nonwoven fabric, 80-120 GSM. Other materials: laminated BOPP-coated PP spunbond for water resistance, PET spunbond for recycled content, and spunlace polyester for premium soft bags.

**What GSM should I use for non-woven bags?**

Standard shopping bags: 80 GSM. Heavy-duty grocery bags: 100-120 GSM. Exhibition and luxury bags: 120-150 GSM with lamination. Below 60 GSM is too weak for regular shopping use. Favourite Fab supplies 80-150 GSM PP spunbond for bag making.

**How much does non-woven bag raw material cost in India?**

PP spunbond 80-120 GSM (standard bag grade): Rs 90-130/kg at bulk pricing. A standard 30x25cm bag uses ~40g fabric = Rs 4-6 material cost per bag at bulk rates. Laminated BOPP adds Rs 2-4 per bag for water resistance.

**Are non-woven bags biodegradable?**

Standard PP spunbond non-woven bags are NOT biodegradable – they are polypropylene plastic. However, they are reusable (100+ times) and recyclable. PLA-based nonwoven bags (from corn starch) are biodegradable but cost 3-4x more.

**Where can I source non-woven bag fabric in bulk in India?**

Favourite Fab (Agra) supplies PP spunbond for bag making: 60-200 GSM, width 1600-3200mm, custom print lamination available. MOQ 500 kg. B2B pricing for bag converters, exporters and retailers.

## Bag Styles: D-Cut, W-Cut and U-Cut Raw Material Requirements

Each non woven bag style places different demands on the raw material. The fabric is the same family — 100% PP spunbond, supplied un-laminated or BOPP-laminated in gloss or matte finish — but the GSM you order should match the bag construction, because handle style and load path determine how much fabric weight the bag needs.

- **D-cut shopping bag** — 50–70 GSM. The die-cut handle is part of the bag body, so the fabric itself carries the load; mid-range GSM gives the handle area enough tear resistance.
- **W-cut grocery bag** — 40–60 GSM. The vest-style handle spreads load across a wider section, allowing lighter fabric for cost-sensitive volume production.
- **U-cut handmade bag** — lightweight fabric around 20 GSM, commonly supplied in 63-inch rolls for hand-made bag stitching units.
- **Loop-handle and box bag** — 80–100 GSM. Attached handles and squared gussets need a stiffer, heavier substrate to hold shape.
- **Laminated promotional bag** — 80–110 GSM with BOPP gloss or matte lamination for high-quality printed graphics.
- **Wedding and sweet-box bag** — 90–110 GSM laminated, where print finish and structure both matter.
- **Heavy-duty industrial bag** — 100–120 GSM for maximum load capacity.

For machine-made bags, the roll must also suit automatic bag-making lines: uniform GSM across the web, calibrated edge tension, and custom slit widths (10–240 cm) on standard 3-inch cores keep high-speed D-cut and W-cut machines running without web breaks or misfeeds. Confirm your bag style, target GSM, and machine width when specifying material so the supplier can slit rolls to your exact converting setup.
